nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Short alpine summers with strong light drive plant growth above the tree line.

nodes.name: Snow & glacier melt
nodes.desc: The park holds glaciers such as the Pasterze; winter snow cover and summer meltwater shape which plants grow and where animals can feed.

nodes.name: Rain & meltwater
nodes.desc: Water from rain and melting snow feeds streams and waterfalls such as the Krimml Waterfalls and keeps the alpine meadows watered.

nodes.name: Alpine soil
nodes.desc: Thin mountain soils hold the nutrients that meadow plants and dwarf shrubs draw on.

nodes.name: Fungi, soil animals & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Rusty-leaved alpenrose
nodes.desc: A dwarf evergreen shrub that, according to Wikipedia, dominates the zone above the tree line in the park.

nodes.name: Bilberry
nodes.desc: A low berry shrub of mountain heath and woodland edges. Red deer and hares are recorded eating it.

nodes.name: Mat-grass
nodes.desc: A tough tussock grass of acidic alpine pastures and meadows.

nodes.name: Alpine meadow-grass
nodes.desc: A common grass of high mountain meadows, grazed by insects and small mammals.

nodes.name: Alpine marmot
nodes.desc: Colonial burrowing rodent that eats grasses, herbs and some insects, and hibernates for up to nine months. Wikipedia notes it was reintroduced to the park area.

nodes.name: Alpine ibex
nodes.desc: Grazer of steep rocky slopes and high meadows, eating mostly grass and adding dwarf shrubs in autumn and winter. Golden eagles may take young.

nodes.name: Chamois
nodes.desc: Mountain goat-antelope and one of the main large mammals of the park, grazing alpine meadows and shrubs.

nodes.name: Red deer
nodes.desc: One of the main large herbivores of the park, eating shrubs such as bilberry as well as grasses.

nodes.name: Mountain hare
nodes.desc: Small herbivore of high ground, recorded eating bilberry; prey of foxes, stoats and golden eagles.

nodes.name: European snow vole
nodes.desc: Small rodent of rocky alpine ground that eats grasses and other plants.

nodes.name: Common green grasshopper
nodes.desc: A grass-feeding grasshopper of meadows, recorded in the area.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: Generalist predator that hunts marmots, hares, voles and insects at all elevations.

nodes.name: Stoat
nodes.desc: Small weasel that hunts voles and other small mammals.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: Omnivorous crow that eats insects and also feeds on carcasses.

nodes.name: Griffon vulture
nodes.desc: Soaring scavenger that Wikipedia lists among the park raptors; feeds on carcasses of large mammals.

nodes.name: Bearded vulture
nodes.desc: Specialist scavenger living mostly on bone and marrow from carcasses. Reintroduced to the Alps from 1987 and now breeding again.

nodes.name: Golden eagle
nodes.desc: Top aerial predator of the Alps, nesting near the tree line and hunting alpine pastures for marmots and hares.
